CARRIER WARNING: thestar.com.my is NOT an approved domain. This is the Reuters wire (Khalid Abdelaziz), Sept 30 dateline, carried 1 October 2026 00:17 MYT. The canonical reuters.com URL was not captured this session — hunt for it on reuters.com before use.

A US ceasefire proposal to pause Sudan's civil war could push the country towards a Libya-style partition in its current form, a top adviser to Sudan's army-led authorities told Reuters, in some of the strongest criticism by a Sudanese official of the plan so far.
The proposal, put forward by US Senior Advisor for Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos, would impose a 90-day ceasefire, followed by negotiations to end the war and resume the move to civilian rule.
QUOTE (unnamed senior adviser to Sudan's army-led authorities, speaking from New York where he attended the General Assembly): "Mr Boulos seems to be putting pressure on us to accept a de facto partitioning of the country similar to [the] Libyan model."
Since last year the RSF has been trying to establish its own parallel government in the city of Nyala in western Darfur. Ministers have been appointed and some police are active, though they have not set up public services or institutions such as schools, hospitals and courts.
